ac:layout-cell.p: Solution Summary · Logical Feature Specification · Feature landing page

This companion to SPEC-SEI-002 assesses existing FR capabilities, Spain changes, product impact and coverage gaps by public and private platform. Business requirements, phase gates and ONB/OFR meanings remain in SPEC-SEI-019. Eight proposed scenario sequences now link the existing operations and Spain qualification gates. The predecessor, source contracts and publication selection remain unchanged.

Audience: architects and engineers. Assess what existing capabilities can be reused, what Spain needs to change, and what evidence remains open. Start with public solution, private solutions and shared Spain differences. Use the scenario sequences to review the proposed interactions. Operation/source detail supports the assessments; new API design remains outside scope.

Agreed direction, 22 October 2026: reuse the existing FR APIs and tailor Spain through the country pack. The scenario sequences below propose reuse of documented operations and explicitly unbound logical handoffs. New endpoint and payload design remains outside scope. Engineering must establish whether each Spain difference needs configuration, a country/provider binding, a shared capability change or a contract extension. REF-REUSE; REF-COUNTRY.

The intended Spain use is to confirm or establish selected public/private functions for a business through Sage. Phase 1 remains public readiness. Later private setup and activation retain their existing gates; Private A to Private B remains disabled. REF-LOGICAL sections 3 and 6.

INT-DS01 adds dataset provisioning; INT-AP01–06 add connect/update, disconnection, ownership, errors, addresses, environments and events. These supplied guides describe partner/internal integration behaviour, not replacement OpenAPI contracts. Ownership and error attachments were duplicated; each identical pair is counted once. Tax/Connections/AFL are implementation reuse candidates under SPEC-SEI-001. The shared onboarding flow is a proposed design pattern. Deployed builds, provider coverage and Spain compatibility remain Unknown until qualified.

Use the shared glossary. Shared behaviour is Reusable with country binding unless the evidence establishes otherwise. Spain rules are Country-specific. Implementation fitness remains Unknown until the owner supplies evidence.

POST /datasets

Guide: start with 202 Accepted, no body; repeat identical input under the same idempotency semantics until completion returns 200 OK. Required header is X-Idempotency-Key; request media type is application/json.
Reuse candidate for the selected direct API channel. Spain public applicability and supported business types remain open; dataset creation is not public-platform enrolment.

ac:layout-cell.p: These are proposed reuse views for architects and engineers, one per ONB-S01–08. SEI019 remains authoritative for business behaviour. The participants are Product, E-Invoice API, Identity, Tax Service and the selected platform. Each view omits unused participants. The platform lane represents the selected public or private platform for that step. These are logical responsibility groups; the diagrams do not approve service placement. Spain country rules appear as condition notes.

Read the labels: Existing shows the documented HTTP method, complete path and success response from FR-01–05 or INT-DS01. Line breaks only wrap a path; they do not change it. Spain deployment/compatibility still needs evidence. To qualify marks a logical handoff with no confirmed contract. Its request and return labels describe intended behaviour; they are not endpoint or payload designs.

Solid arrows are requests. Dashed arrows are paired responses. Grey activation bars show handling intervals, with no promised duration or synchronous provider completion. HTTP success does not establish readiness or activation. Provider timing, events and observation freshness remain subject to section 5.

Each diagram assumes authorised business/dataset access and the correct environment. opt marks conditional work. Steps after a gate run only if its prerequisites pass; failed or unknown evidence returns an owned hold under ONB-08. Dataset creation is conditional on the channel and is never public-platform enrolment. INT-DS01's two POST requests show the successful create/confirm path with the same input and X-Idempotency-Key; repeat limits and recovery still need qualification.

ac:layout-cell.h3: 4.4 Spain NIF, establishments and dataset mapping
ac:layout-cell.p: France identifies a legal unit with SIREN and an establishment with SIRET, which contains that SIREN plus an establishment identifier. FR-OBS01 therefore shows two addresses for the same SIREN, not evidence of two legal units. REF-FR-IDS.

tr.td: Taxpayer versus establishment

Article 22 assigns NIF to legal persons/entities. Its composition identifies entity category, a number and a control character; it does not define a SIRET-style establishment suffix. Local/premises details are recorded separately in the census. Keep establishment or provider-routing references separate from NIF; do not invent a child-NIF format. REF-ES-NIF, REF-ES-NIF-FORM, REF-ES-LOCALES.
Separately identified permanent establishment

A nonresident entity’s permanent establishments with clearly different activities and separate management must obtain NIFs distinct from the nonresident entity under Article 22(2). These are independent identifiers, not a prefix-derived hierarchy. Qualify this scope explicitly; do not infer parent/child relationships from matching NIF characters. REF-ES-NIF.
Accountant, company group and dataset

A commercial group or accountant portfolio is separate from the represented taxpayer and address. Open: one NIF/multiple addresses and multiple NIFs under a dataset need actual country/provider and isolation evidence. NIF rules do not choose dataset cardinality. Keep authority, certificate purpose and results scoped to the represented business; no portfolio-wide grant follows from shared technical access. GAP-01/02/03; REF-LOGICAL ONB-R04/19.
